Simple geometric figures are typically perceived to be more pleasant than complex ones, whereas complex ones are typically perceived to be more interesting than simple ones.

questions.evidenceQuote: In one experiment, Berlyne manipulated two factors of geometric figures: the first was symmetry (i.e., how symmetrical and homogeneous elements were), and the other was the number of elements (i.e., one to five elements vs. numerous elements). Some figures were simple and symmetrical, some were simple and asymmetrical, some were complex and symmetrical, and the others were complex and asymmetrical. Participants rated the simple and symmetrical figures to be the most pleasant, followed by complex and symmetrical, simple and asymmetrical, and complex and asymmetrical. Symmetry was key to pleasantness.

questions.evidenceQuote: These paintings are quite shocking and grotesque, particularly in comparison to the famously serene, warm painting by Monet. After looking at each painting, participants reported how interesting or uninteresting, boring or engaging, enjoyable or unenjoyable, pleasing or displeasing, comprehensible or incomprehensible, familiar or unfamiliar each painting was. Results showed that pleasantness ratings were predicted by comprehensibleness, familiarity, and simpleness. In other words, the easier to understand and simpler the paintings were, the more pleasant they were.

questions.evidenceQuote: In another experiment, Silvia explored the role of comprehension. For instance, participants were asked to read Scott MacLeod’s famously abstract poem The Life of Haifisch. Those who were not provided with any background information could not understand it and did not find it interesting. In contrast, the other participants who read the same poem but with more background information, such as its title and the explanation that Haifisch means “shark” in German, found it more comprehensible and far more interesting.

So we asked over 5,000 people about their reading habits during childhood, their current cognitive styles, and their perceived levels of psychological richness.

These readers seemed to “essentialize” to a greater degree than those who had read less romance.

specificFindings: The Rothko continuation is quoted with the already-evidenced Looking at prefix so the visceral response has its actual subject. Visceral is a deeply felt experience,not a medical condition or physical entry into a painting.

Repeated sitting before No13 and Metropolitan Museum of Art are author autobiographical details,not a current exhibition listing or purchase claim. The two abbreviation-split IDs support distinct action and location questions using the same complete original sentence.

Draws me in describes attention absorption. The neighbouring maybe and or maybe prevent asserting that knowing the artists life certainly causes the response. No new diagnostic claim about the artist or reader is added.

Berlynes1971 book summarizes a series of experiments. Simple-versus-complex typical pleasantness and interestingness directions are kept separate,with typically not converted into every individual always responding identically.
The geometric design crosses symmetry with element quantity. Simple/complex and symmetrical/asymmetrical are two different factors; no colour,price or unreported random assignment is invented.
Pleasantness ranking is simple symmetrical,complex symmetrical,simple asymmetrical,complex asymmetrical. The second-ranked condition is not confused with the first or with an interestingness ranking.

Symmetry important to pleasantness does not imply it was the only manipulated factor or made the figures most interesting. Complexity/asymmetry increase one rated dimension while reducing the other in the reported comparison.

Silvia and Samuel Turner Jr form the later experiment team. Jr is a name suffix,not the actual end of a sentence. The same full sentence binds the subsequent conducted predicate,with separate attribution and topic questions.
More recently is relative to the source book,not a claim to have checked current literature. Painting experiments,poem comprehension experiment and later retrospective reading survey remain separate.
Shocking/grotesque is contrasted with Monets serene warmth without requiring names absent from the current parent. Film,artist and participant roles are not exchanged.

After each painting,participants self-report several bipolar dimensions. These are not objective art-history tests,one overall enjoyment score or a pre-view single-image recall task; those distractors were refined before review.

Pleasantness predicted by comprehension,familiarity,simplicity is distinguished from interestingness predicted by disturbingness/unpleasantness. Statistical prediction among ratings is not rewritten as proven independent deterministic causes.

The poem study concerns comprehension,using the same Scott MacLeod poem with versus without background information. No-background participants reported the described lack of comprehension/interest; the supplied German shark meaning belongs to the informed comparison.

Intricate line is a subtle conceptual boundary. At least minimally comprehensible is a necessary threshold in the authors discussion,not a numerical universal cutoff or a sufficient condition that all easy art is rich.

Existing literature in the Virginia collaboration means research publications,not solely fiction. Westgate and Buttrick are two students at the books described stage,not independently verified present roles.
We wondered if introduces a question followed by asking more than5000 people about childhood reading,current cognition and perceived richness. It is not childhood random assignment or causal proof.
We assumed and would be associated with are initial expectations,not the findings. More intricate in the next sentence stops the initial broad hypothesis replacing the actual results.

Romance readers seemed to essentialize more than those who read less romance. Seemed,degree and comparator remain intact; no diagnosis of all romance readers or genre-causes-inflexibility conclusion is made.

Joe,Jill,baseball and opera are illustrative simplistic labels,not verified moral assessments of named actual participants or the authors commands about taste. Tended preserves a group tendency and the reading studies are correlational.

Final question evidence is only its target example sentence,leaving later unassigned material for future authorship. Planned-evidence guard confirms exactly25 added IDs and no published fingerprints changed.
